label: Checked rather than accepted, as asked. Seed 4, sizes 16 and 32, 300 s, dry.
inference_tested: that none of the six earlier inert verdicts is affected by the representation/placement logging gap, because all six act through stream admission, robot admission, ordering or declining.
verdict: THE INFERENCE HOLDS FOR ALL SIX, but for s6-decline it holds for a DIFFERENT REASON than the one given, and that difference is a live warning for the pressure run.

builder-s1-feasible.channel: act.streams, which reaches _serve_monitor and logs as release_monitor rows

builder-s2-all.channel: RecallAction.decision CLOUD against DEVICE/DEFER; CLOUD logs release_recall, DEVICE/REJECT log decline, DEFER logs defer

builder-s4-llf.channel: CHECKED SPECIFICALLY because Action.order is itself a dead channel. It is not acting through order: arms_builder.py:186-189 builds candidates with key (dl - svc) for llf against dl for edf and SORTS THE RELEASE LIST, a live path. Its null is therefore genuinely cancelled-by-geometry, not an instrument null. It does also set the dead order label at :164, but the live sort is what carries the mechanism.

builder-s6-decline.blindness: coordinator.py:446-455 puts DEVICE and REJECT in the SAME BRANCH: same state, same served_at, same answer record, and both log _log_decision(t, "decline", ...). decision.jsonl cannot tell them apart. outcomes.jsonl does record `decision`, so the question is settleable today.
builder-s6-decline.why_the_verdict_still_stands: the branch is never reached. The arm emits CLOUD on EVERY recall at both sizes, 21 of 21 at n=16 and 42 of 42 at n=32, identically for builder-default and builder-s6-decline, so no DEVICE or REJECT is ever emitted and there is nothing for the log to be blind to.
builder-s6-decline.latent_risk: THE BLINDNESS IS LATENT, NOT ABSENT. If the pressure work loads the recall axis as intended, s6-decline will begin emitting DEVICE and REJECT, and at that moment a decision-row diff becomes blind to it. The emitted-action or outcomes.jsonl observable must be used for s6-decline in any pressured cell.

shared_cause_reconfirmed: s2-all, s2-value, s6-decline and s7-degrade are inert for ONE reason, now confirmed directly: every recall is feasible, so the arm emits CLOUD on all of them and no admission, declining or degradation branch is ever reached.

two_kinds_of_null_now_both_observed.workload_null: s7-degrade and s6-decline. The arm own condition never holds and its own counters read zero. Evidence about the workload.
two_kinds_of_null_now_both_observed.instrument_null: builder-s7-always-recent first result. The arm fired on every recall and decision.jsonl has no representation column. Evidence about the log.
two_kinds_of_null_now_both_observed.why_it_matters: the two look identical in a results table and only the first is evidence about the mechanism. One of each has now been found, which is why they are labelled separately rather than both as "inert".

control_construction.rule: a control must be CONSTRUCTED by disabling the change, not by APPROXIMATING its absence.
compliance_of_my_own_work: builder-s7-degrade and builder-s7-always-recent against builder-default: a single s7 slot flag gates the whole mechanism and every other slot is identical through the same _mk constructor. Constructed, not approximated.

the eco-llm reconciliation: the BEFORE arm had the new _rep_tokens REPLACED at runtime by the exact prior function, so the control is the change switched off rather than a configuration believed equivalent to its absence.
control_construction.note: recorded affirmatively rather than assumed, since the rule arrived from a case where a control was a third condition belonging to neither arm.

per_category_note: Two independent routes now agree that per-category effects on this workload are noise and that acting on them is actively harmful rather than merely unhelpful: the statistical collapse on DEV to EVAL, and per-category lookups serving 0 of 35 at n = 16 to 39. This is recorded here because RecallQuery.category (interface.py:112) is the ONLY query-side signal our observation exposes, which bears directly on QueryStream QDP below.

querystream_qdp_status.channel: LIVE since Part A: RecallAction.representation is read by _submit_recall at coordinator.py:552 through cstate.tokens_for_representation.
querystream_qdp_status.signal: ABSENT. QDP prunes tokens by semantic relevance to the query and temporal novelty. RecallQuery exposes query_id, session_id, category, arrival_s, deadline_s, evidence, readiness, readiness_tokens and device_answer_confidence. There is no token-level or frame-level relevance signal, and the only query-side feature is `category`.
querystream_qdp_status.consequence: porting QDP would mean building its selection on `category`, the one signal now shown by two independent routes to be noise and harmful to act on. The blocker has therefore MOVED rather than cleared: it is no longer "the action cannot be taken" but "the decision cannot be made".
querystream_qdp_status.distinction: channel live, signal absent. That is a different class from the three dead channels and should be labelled as such rather than as a port that is merely pending.
